card.title: Lead balls and the density of the Earth

panels.text: The Cavendish experiment, performed in 1797-1798 by Henry Cavendish, was the first experiment to measure the force of gravity between masses in the laboratory.
The apparatus was a torsion balance: a six-foot wooden rod hung horizontally from a wire, with a lead sphere attached to each end.
Two large weights attracted the small weights, causing the beam to rotate slightly.
From this, Cavendish found that the Earth's density was 5.448 times that of water. The current accepted value is 5.514 g/cm³.
